metric: Debian popcon installations of the lead's runtime library binary package (max when two sonames are listed)

leads.name: expat
leads.reason: Selected and verified: XML_ParserCreateNS/XML_Parse matched both controls under LLVM source coverage with a stable AFL++ differential; see data/c/xml/parsers.json.

leads.name: libxml2
leads.reason: Selected and verified: xmlReaderForMemory/xmlTextReaderRead matched both controls under LLVM source coverage with a stable AFL++ differential; see data/c/xml/parsers.json. Second on the primary metric (libxml2 binary 290,724 vs libexpat1 297,134, a 2.2% gap; libxml2-16 adds 9,413 on hosts that may also have libxml2) and on the Homebrew cross-check. Independent parser family from expat.

leads.name: mxml
leads.reason: Selected and verified: Mini-XML 4.0.6 mxmlLoadString (opaque text values) matched both controls under LLVM source coverage with a stable AFL++ differential; see data/c/xml/parsers.json. Third on the primary metric (libmxml1 2,054, the 3.x soname; most in no-files). Own parser family. Mini-XML does not implement namespace semantics: the adapter resolves xmlns from mxml's parsed tree.

leads.name: libroxml
leads.reason: No Debian package (no primary or Debian value). Under the C/C++ star fallback blunderer/libroxml has 15 GitHub stars (tags up to 3.0.2), below the 100-star threshold. Not built.

leads.name: yxml

leads.name: ezxml

leads.name: sxmlc

leads.name: libnxml
leads.reason: Selected and verified: nxml_parse_buffer matched the expat non-namespace summary of both valid controls as a raw-name path, with libnxml line coverage and a stable AFL++ differential; see data/c/xml/parsers.json. Own parser family.

leads.name: iksemel
leads.reason: Targeted lookup: libiksemel3 has 4,375 installations in the binary by_inst file, but the iksemel source is no longer in Debian (no sourcemax row; sources.debian.org has no current package). Own SAX/tree parser in C (iks_parse, iks_tree), not namespace-aware. A throwaway raw-name probe of the upstream iksemel-1.4.tar.gz (Google Code archive, SHA-256 458c1b8fb3349076a6cecf26c29db1d561315d84e16bfcfba419f327f502e244, LGPL-2.1) with iks_tree matched the expat non-namespace summary of catalog-ns.xml but not order-default-ns.xml: sax.c decodes only the five predefined entities in text and maps every other reference to '?' (sku text 'A?7', amount '12?50 ?'), and attribute values are not decoded at all (note='say "hi"'). It fails the cell's second valid control, so no project or AFL++ overlay was built.

leads.name: glib2.0 (GMarkup)
leads.reason: Targeted lookup: GLib's GMarkup (g_markup_parse_context_parse, documented at https://docs.gtk.org/glib/method.MarkupParseContext.parse.html) is a C XML-subset parser over local buffers. Its Debian source glib2.0 builds all of GLib, so the runtime counts (libglib2.0-0t64 167,992) are not format-specific, and Debian has no GMarkup-specific development package for the protocol's fallback (libglib2.0-dev 32,154 covers all of GLib). Unranked and not selected. GMarkup is exercised and covered as the underlying parser of the libxmlb path.

leads.name: libgsf
leads.reason: Targeted lookup (libgsf-1-114 86,874). Structured-file I/O library (OLE2, ZIP); its GsfXMLIn wraps libxml2's push SAX parser and dispatches only to elements declared in a caller-supplied GsfXMLInNode table, so it offers no generic element view of an arbitrary document. libxml2 family; excluded like other schema-mapping wrappers.

leads.name: qdbm (Cabin XML helpers)
leads.reason: Targeted lookup (libqdbm14 6,234). Database library; its Cabin utility API has cbxmlbreak/cbxmlattrs, which split a string into tag and text tokens without nesting or tree, so it is a tokenizer helper inside a multi-purpose library, not an XML parser path.

leads.name: xmlrpc-epi
leads.reason: Debian source-name hit (libxmlrpc-epi0 3,518). XML-RPC protocol library over expat; not a general XML parser API. expat family.

leads.name: xmlrpc-c
leads.reason: Debian source-name hit (libxmlrpc-core-c3 1,434). XML-RPC protocol library; parses XML-RPC messages through its bundled expat-derived xmlparse or libxml2; not a general XML parser API.

leads.name: libstrophe
leads.reason: Targeted lookup (libstrophe0 213). XMPP client library; XML stanzas are parsed by expat or libxml2. Protocol library, not a general XML parser API.

leads.name: wbxml2
leads.reason: Debian source-name hit (libwbxml2-0 170). WBXML (binary XML) codec; textual XML goes through expat. Different format and not a general XML parser API.

leads.name: ixml
leads.debian_source: pupnp (formerly libupnp); binaries libixml11t64, libixml10, libixml22
leads.reason: Selected and verified: pupnp 22.2.1 ixmlParseBufferEx matched the expat non-namespace summary of both valid controls as a raw-name path (IXML's own namespaceURI fields are not conformant on the controls), with 1,428 IXML lines covered (908 in ixmlparser.c) and a stable AFL++ differential (433 vs 449 tuples, 82 differing); see data/c/xml/parsers.json. Own parser family.

leads.name: gdome2
leads.search: round-4 targeted Debian binary lookup (C DOM libraries over a selected parser)
leads.reason: Selected and verified: gdome2 0.8.1+debian-10 gdome_di_createDocFromMemory gave the exact namespace-resolved summary of both valid controls through its DOM Level 2 accessors, with 744 gdome2 lines and 3,207 libxml2 lines covered and a stable AFL++ differential (1,389 vs 1,490 tuples, 259 differing); libxml2 family. See data/c/xml/parsers.json.

leads.name: neon
leads.reason: Technically verified in a scratch build on 2026-11-18 (not committed as a project): neon 0.37.1 (notroj.github.io release tarball, SHA-256 a99b7262525a454d1065cf76dd17240fd808dfc4ef15636990ff83a5d0d9e740, LGPL-2.0-or-later) ne_xml_create/ne_xml_push_handler/ne_xml_parse over the pinned libxml2 2.15.4 (Debian builds neon27 --with-libxml2) gave the exact namespace-resolved summary of both controls; neon's ne_xml.c lines are the same on both controls (334 libxml2 parser.c line starts differ), so it would be a libxml2-family wrapper. Not ranked: libneon27t64 is the whole HTTP/WebDAV client library and Debian has no XML-specific neon package, so by the rule this cell applies to GLib's GMarkup its count is not format-specific; libneon27-dev (1,390) is not format-specific either.

leads.name: apr-util (apr_xml)
leads.reason: APR-util's documented apr_xml_parser_create/apr_xml_parser_feed/apr_xml_parser_done builds an apr_xml_doc tree over expat with its own namespace scoping. Not built: libaprutil1t64 is the whole APR utility library and Debian has no XML-specific package, so by the GMarkup rule its count is not format-specific; libaprutil1-dev (1,831) is not format-specific either. Its public tree also hides namespace declarations (apr_xml_ns_scope is private) and stores attributes in reverse order.

leads.name: libxmltok (expat 1.2)
leads.reason: libxmltok_1.2.orig.tar.gz (snapshot.debian.org SHA-1 5dab2918859febf67e0192e0347ad5ca864baa67) unpacks to expat-1.2: James Clark's expat 1.2 (xmltok, xmlrole, xmlparse), the predecessor release of the selected expat with the same XML_Parser API. Whitespace- and comment-normalized non-trivial lines matching expat 2.10.0 in sequence: 3,134 of 6,328 (49.5%; xmltok_impl.c 77.5%, xmlparse.c 35.7%). Below the ~70% fork threshold only because expat 2 was rewritten around the same code; it is the same project at a 2000 release, not a distinct package API, so it is excluded rather than counted as a second expat-family path.

leads.name: libxml (1.x)
leads.reason: GNOME libxml 1.x, the predecessor of the selected libxml2; no current source. Predecessor path; not counted.

leads.name: libucw-xml
leads.reason: Selected and verified: LibUCW 6.5 ucw-xml (xml_init, xml_ns_enable, xml_push_fastbuf, xml_next pull loop) gave the exact namespace-resolved summary of both valid controls; 804 ucw-xml lines covered (387 in parse.c); stable AFL++ differential (501 vs 544 tuples, 87 differing). Own parser family.

leads.name: rxp
leads.search: round-4 targeted Debian binary lookup (C parsers named in XML parser comparisons)
leads.reason: Selected and verified: RXP 1.5.0 (Debian orig plus Debian patches) NewParser/ParserSetFlag(XMLNamespaces)/ReadXBit gave the shared namespace-resolved summary of both valid controls without a declaration count (RXP returns no xmlns declarations); 2,544 RXP lines covered (987 in xmlparser.c); stable AFL++ differential (903 vs 942 tuples, 119 differing). Own parser family; 16 installations are a very weak signal.

leads.name: xml.c
leads.reason: Star-fallback candidate (225 stars, tag release-0.2.0, MIT): xml_parse_document returns NULL on both valid controls because it parses tags without attributes; it also has no CDATA or entity decoding (data/c/xml/xmlc-lead-check.json).

debian_search.note: Leads above the three selected paths were added from the Debian source-name search ('xml', 306 hits, 5 C XML parser libraries) and targeted lookups; all other hits are classified in the snapshot.
